selected_problem: Fresh main aligned changeset and federated regular-file identities for trailing separators, but semantic graph normalization still preserved src/a.js/ as distinct from src/a.js and also allowed spellings such as ./ to collapse to an empty semantic file identity.
decision_basis: This is a direct path-identity consistency gap exposed by the fresh-main changeset/federated invariants, not a new architecture choice.
The semantic graph already canonicalizes slashes, dot segments and parent segments before node identity, so trailing-separator collapse belongs to the same lexical identity boundary.
Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained unavailable with transient HTTP 502; this cycle uses DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY and does not claim a hosted DWAC success receipt.

pre_fix_reality.empty_identity: ./ normalized to an empty semantic node path

change: Semantic graph path normalization now removes trailing separators after POSIX lexical normalization and fails closed on empty/dot identities. Identical src/a.js and src/a.js/ inputs collapse to one node; conflicting contents reuse the existing SEMANTIC_PATH_CONTENT_CONFLICT gate.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: PASS: standalone Node reproduction of fresh-main normalization returned distinct plain/trailing identities and an empty identity for ./.
validation.node_check: PASS on the exact proposed semantic-repo-graph module content used for focused replay.
validation.focused_tests: 3/3 PASS: identical alias collapse, conflicting alias fail-closed, and empty identity rejection.

truth_boundary: This closes trailing-separator and empty lexical identities in the in-memory semantic file model. It does not claim filesystem case/Unicode equivalence, parser-grade module resolution, exhaustive large-repository coverage, or arbitrary complex repository synthesis.
